video_title: Dame Revives Portland | Who’s Really a Contender in the East?

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Damian Lillard's impact on the Portland Trail Blazers' early success
quotes.excerpt: to see Dame doing what he does, especially hitting the deep threes, is like nothing you've ever seen
quotes.quote: You think you've seen normal NBA superstars' spectacles when you've seen guys come into town. But to see Dame doing what he does, especially hitting the deep threes, like he did in that first game against the Thunder, is like nothing you've ever seen before. I've always been someone who's like, a star ages out of a certain point of his career and it's fine to just let them go. But this has been such a unique, special experience. You feel the specialness as he's going through those possessions. And they've been really good, and I think a lot of that is a credit to the synchronicity that he has with Deni Avdija specifically.

quotes.speaker: Rob Mahoney

text_blocks.speaker: Rob Mahoney
text_blocks.text: To fully measure the force of what we're talking about, for those not familiar with our three podcasting work together, Justin's cold, cold heart has been thawed by this Dame iteration. That is one of the surprises of the season.

text_blocks.speaker: Justin Verrier
text_blocks.text: It's true. And also, when you watch the Blazers play, you're absolutely right. It's impossible not to feel the atmosphere, the connection. How many situations are there where you had that decade-plus long relationship between star and city, much less a player of Dame's caliber? And so when he comes back, returns to pretty good form, does look more or less like himself, it's a powerful thing for neutral fans and neutral observers, much less anyone with a stake in that team.

quotes.summary_phrase: Damian Lillard's return to form and impact on Portland's atmosphere
quotes.excerpt: when he comes back, returns to pretty good form, does look more or less like himself, it's a powerful thing

quotes.speaker: Rob Mahoney
quotes.summary_phrase: The unique skill sets of veteran stars like Damian Lillard and Ja Morant
quotes.excerpt: what they could do just by craft and angles and just feeling the court
quotes.quote: I've got a new-found respect from some of these superstars once they've been beset by injuries or time has gone by. Not only Dame, but also with Ja Morant. The processing skills that they have once the athletic pop just isn't there, what they could do just by craft and angles and just feeling the court. And that's the whole thing about this Blazers team to begin with, is there's just widespread feel and flow to all of their offense.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Scoot Henderson's struggles and the emergence of Cidy Cissoko
quotes.excerpt: they've replaced Scoot with Cidy Cissoko. You talk about star and city, Cidy is sudokuing him
quotes.quote: Recently, they've flipped from Ja to Scoot. Scoot didn't play well, he's back on the bench, and they've replaced Scoot with Cidy Cissoko. You talk about star and city, Cidy is sudokuing him. He is the puzzle, you know, that's his nickname now. But no, he just brings a ton of energy and good things happen for it and you've seen this team work as a collective.

quotes.speaker: Rob Mahoney
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of Damian Lillard and Deni Avdija on Portland's offense
quotes.excerpt: specifically, Dame and Deni playing off of each other, then everything kind of falling in line
quotes.quote: It really has been Dame and Deni playing off of each other, then everything kind of falling in line from there. To fully measure the force of what we're talking about, for those not familiar with our three podcasting work together, Justin's cold, cold heart has been thawed by this Dame iteration. That is one of the surprises of the season.

quotes.speaker: Rob Mahoney
quotes.summary_phrase: The Philadelphia 76ers as the top contender in the Eastern Conference
quotes.excerpt: I have one team in the top tier of the Eastern Conference. I have labeled the real deal, and it is the Philadelphia 76ers
quotes.quote: I have one team in the top tier of the Eastern Conference. I have labeled the real deal, and it is the Philadelphia 76ers. I know they play with their food. I know the point differential is not there. I know the rotation isn't great. I know Joel Embiid sometimes looks like a wreck league lifer with a bad back. All of those things are true. I have already seen enough to believe that they will flip whatever switches need to be flipped, they will respond in game in whatever manner necessary. They just have been so compelling as a team that has all of that resourcefulness between their stars where they will shift balance in terms of who's creating, they'll shift balance in terms of how they're guarding.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: The Philadelphia 76ers' potential as a championship-level team
quotes.excerpt: the fact that they could plug and play Joel and Paul all over the floor defensively
quotes.quote: I want to believe that the Sixers can be the Sixers again. I want to believe that this version of the Celtics is what we're going to see all season. And I want to believe that between Kade taking another kind of mini step up, a Sar Thompson, who I do think has been a little snappier in terms of the way he's reading the weird coverages on the floor and helping connect the dots of the offense, and eventually getting Jalen Duren back, I want to believe that that can work. And I think there's enough reason to think that they're at least here and not hanging out with the Cavs and the Hawks and whoever else you want to talk about.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Scotty Barnes' defensive growth and All-Defensive potential
quotes.excerpt: Scotty Barnes is finally an all-defensive worthy kind of guy after three years of people saying it.
quotes.quote: Scotty Barnes is finally an all-defensive worthy kind of guy after three years of people saying it and then not actually happening on the court. He is actually that guy now. You cannot be Kawhi Leonard who is in his prime and is just straight up a top-five offense. Just put me anywhere, it is top-five offense because we do not turn the ball over and I just create incredible shots all day long. Scotty Barnes is not that, but Scotty Barnes is a one-on-one threat. You cannot just have any little cross-match up on a switch and think, no, it will be fine, Scotty Barnes has the ball. No. If the wrong guy is guarding him, he is going to make you pay consistently.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Scotty Barnes' mid-range scoring volume and efficiency
quotes.excerpt: Scotty Barnes number two in the league in mid-range scoring by volume shooting 51% from mid-range.
quotes.quote: When people would compare Scotty Barnes as the next Kawhi Leonard, you would stop, you would laugh. And I would like to point you in the direction this year, mid-range scoring. Scotty Barnes number two in the league in mid-range scoring by volume shooting 51% from mid-range.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Comparing Scottie Barnes to Kawhi Leonard's offensive profile
quotes.excerpt: You cannot be Kawhi Leonard who is in his prime and is just straight up a top-five offense.
quotes.quote: You cannot be Kawhi Leonard who is in his prime and is just straight up a top-five offense. Just put me anywhere, it is top-five offense because we do not turn the ball over and I just create incredible shots all day long. Scotty Barnes is not that, but Scotty Barnes is a one-on-one threat. You cannot just have any little cross-match up on a switch and think, no, it will be fine, Scotty Barnes has the ball. No. If the wrong guy is guarding him, he is going to make you pay consistently.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors' decision-making when stars are off the floor
quotes.excerpt: The points where they've looked the worst are the decision-making when they have neither Scottie nor Kawhi.
quotes.quote: The Raptors haven't looked great all the time, but I think the points where they've looked the worst are the decision-making when they have neither Scottie nor Kawhi out there. The moments where it's like we're just going to try to balance this with RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley, it just doesn't work. There is a lot of hope in the idea that when they do have those two stars properly staggered, that they're going to be good enough defensively, and those two are going to be so immutable in terms of the shots they can create. That's a really good team. That's a really dangerous team.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Raptors' defensive versatility and size-down strategy
quotes.excerpt: Their ability to defend while size down is going to be a nice little counter-punch.
quotes.quote: Their ability to defend while size down is going to be a nice little counter-punch to a lot of these teams that are kind of relying on size. I think the Sixers in particular where it's like, Joel Embiid, get your ass on the other end of the floor and run with us in a way that the Raptors can. I also think Kawhi is like at this stage of his career, even if he isn't going to be peak Kawhi in the way that he was last season, he needs to be there to take attention off of Scottie because you've seen how good he is within the flow of things. As the more the defensive attention comes, that's why I think he's probably best suited as a top-tier number two than he is like a clear-cut number one.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Pistons' lack of playoff potential
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons will not make the NBA finals under any circumstance. There's no way they make the finals.
quotes.quote: The Pistons will not make the NBA finals under any circumstance. There's no way they make the finals. Do you think there's a chance they make the conference finals? No. Fuck no. Zero percent chance they make the conference finals. They play the Knicks, Celtics or Sixers in the second round, they're getting their asses kicked.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Sixers' vulnerability to injury and reliance on Embiid
quotes.excerpt: The Sixers could be devastated by injury and they're particularly vulnerable.
quotes.quote: The Sixers could be devastated by injury and they're particularly vulnerable. It's more that now LeBron James has to play 44 minutes a game and I don't know that anyone wants him doing that including LeBron James. Jabari Walker, I mean look, we did kind of skate past Jabari Walker, crucial backup big for the Philadelphia 76ers. I'm a Dominic Barlow guy too. Listen, Detroit played, I give Detroit a 0% chance against the Knicks, Celtics or Sixers in the second round matchup. It's disrespectful not only to the Sixers but to America's heartland.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's belief in the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: Donovan Mitchell believes in this team even if you don't.
quotes.quote: I just went on their website earlier this morning and it said Donovan Mitchell believes in this team even if you don't. And I laughed to myself. I was like, yeah, nigga, I don't. I don't believe in you. We don't believe in you.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: James Harden's defensive effort and role adjustment
quotes.excerpt: Harden's like kvetching, like he's like there's still comments coming out.
quotes.quote: Harden's like kvetching, like he's like there's still comments coming out. It wasn't just him and Kenny Atkinson getting into it on the court. It's like he's also making allusions to the fact that, uh, they don't need me as a scorer anymore, so I guess I'm going to have to play make. That's the Donovan Mitchell zone, okay? I get it, you don't want me. It's like, no shit. Like you base plans in the playoffs and you can't get past anyone on the perimeter.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' defensive struggles and personnel issues
quotes.excerpt: This Cavs team that is not good did just beat the Knicks. Harden dropped 32.
quotes.quote: To be clear, this Cavs team that is not good did just beat the Knicks. Yeah, Harden dropped 32, which again, it's just like anytime that's happening, you know nobody's taking that game serious. They're dead inside. It is how I look at it. They're done and I think that's the human component that for instance, I didn't factor in most. I had them as in the finals going into this year because I was just like, the Cavs. He did. I know. It was bad. We tried to throw our bodies in front of it and it didn't work.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' over-reliance on individual effort
quotes.excerpt: I made the same mistake with the Cavs that I did the Magic.
quotes.quote: I made the same mistake with the Cavs that I did the Magic, because I overestimated how little needs to happen in order for them to get over the hump. But what that little is, is just like so baked into who they are as people and like how much they've hit their head against the wall and how tired they are of this scenario, that like that's the only thing that matters at this point.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Lack of belief in the Cavaliers' playoff potential
quotes.excerpt: No chance. There's just no belief in the Cavs. Just no.
quotes.quote: No chance. There's just no belief in the Cavs. Just no. They will have, I believe in the human condition to change, okay? To get better. Man's capacity to change, yeah. Yes. Yeah, I'm not seeing that. Some of us have it, a lot of us don't. The Cavs are on the don't side.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Heat's defensive struggles and roster concerns
quotes.excerpt: They're a bottom five defense in Adam Silver's NBA. Bam Adebayo, Erik Spoelstra, Davion Mitchell, Giannis Antetokounmpo.
quotes.quote: I wanted to talk to you about a team that none of us, even contemplated putting in this hypothetical at all, and that's the Miami Heat who they fucking stink, y'all. They're a bottom five defense in Adam Silver's NBA. Bam Adebayo, Erik Spoelstra, Davion Mitchell, Giannis Antetokounmpo. Bottom five defense in the NBA. They're getting smoked on that end and nobody thinks this is going to be some like, oh no, they'll be like one of the good teams soon. No. They're just going to stink this year.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Heat's defensive improvement and offensive concerns
quotes.excerpt: They are putting a lid on the basket defensively, especially of late.
quotes.quote: There have been better indicators of late. Now they have been on a West Coast trip and they're playing a lot of the dregs of the league like they beat up on the Kings and all of a sudden things look better. But like, they are putting a lid on the basket defensively, especially of late. And I do wonder if that's going to filter out like maybe the three-point shooting success kind of goes the other way and maybe they're like decent to good on that end, but the bigger concern is just like on the opposite end at that point because Giannis is scoring at the basket.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's offensive consistency and team needs
quotes.excerpt: Giannis is scoring at the basket. Giannis has been fine because Giannis is always fine.
quotes.quote: Giannis is scoring at the basket. Giannis has been fine because Giannis is always fine because he does the same thing, right? Nobody else is putting pressure on the rim outside of that and I just don't know how they put together a credible offense once the defense balances out and I do think the defense is going to balance out. When like, what does James Harden do? Like, just like he's already made a lot of sacrifices to his game. I just like he has to be a different player and I think they're going to have to look themselves very hard in the mirror and determine whether or not they want to move someone like James Harden in order to make this team better fit Giannis.

quotes.speaker: Justin Verrier
quotes.summary_phrase: Hope for Heat's defense versus offensive limitations
quotes.excerpt: I do think there's clearly more hope for the defense than the offense.
quotes.quote: I mean I do think there's clearly more hope for the defense than the offense just by virtue of the personnel, but it it feels like the kind of defense that even though it will have successful stretches will always feel a little wobbly. And you can see it now where it's not like effort is the problem. Like they're trying. They're trying to fix this. But this personnel and I would even say defensively, them trying to fix it has become part of the problem in itself where then they over-rotate, they over-commit, it creates a whole different other cascading set of problems.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's leadership and team dynamics
quotes.excerpt: Giannis's whole thing is like, I have to play this one way.
quotes.quote: Giannis's whole thing is like, I have to play this one way. And it's understandable. You've won MVPs and defensive and blah blah blah blah blah. But the best players adapt. You know, even, you know, you can say whatever you want about LeBron. Old, he's old as fuck. So, he should have been doing this. But last year that stretch was just like, yo, LeBron doesn't shoot or handle anymore. He just sets good screens, finishes plays. Then the playoffs come, Luka's out, they beat the fucking the the Rockets that they should have no business beating in the first round.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's leadership and team adaptation
quotes.excerpt: He has to be a different player and I think they're going to have to look themselves.
quotes.quote: He has to be a different player and I think they're going to have to look themselves very hard in the mirror and determine whether or not they want to move someone like James Harden in order to make this team better fit Giannis. Because otherwise, I just don't know how you can take them seriously. I I mean I do think there's clearly more hope for the defense than the offense just by virtue of the personnel, but it it feels like the kind of defense that even though it will have successful stretches will always feel a little wobbly.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's leadership and team adaptation
quotes.excerpt: As a superstar, it's your job to make people better, to pick them up where they fall.
quotes.quote: As a superstar, it's your job to make people better, to pick them up where they fall. And it just feels like Giannis doesn't do that for anyone. He's not a good leader. He hasn't been for a very long time.

quotes.speaker: Rob Perez
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's leadership style versus team success
quotes.excerpt: This is the difference between his style of leadership and someone like Dame's.
quotes.quote: I think I mean this is the difference between his style of leadership and someone like Dame's, right? Is that like comprehensive team lifting effect and maybe that's a little warm and fuzzy for the likings of some basketball fans, but you see it in the intangibles of a team. You need a rest. Sometimes that's what deference looks like, you know?
